title: Scroll Compressor Installation Manual — Rev C
sourceText: Before installing the scroll compressor, verify that the suction line and discharge pressure gauges are connected correctly. Low superheat readings may indicate a refrigerant charge issue. Allow the condensing unit to equalize for 15 minutes before startup.

title: Condenser Fan Replacement — Quick Reference Card
sourceText: If the condenser fan does not spin freely, disconnect power at the unit before servicing. Inspect the evaporator coil for frost buildup, which can signal a subcooling imbalance.

title: Refrigerant Safety Data Sheet — Web Page Copy
sourceText: Always store refrigerant cylinders upright in a ventilated area. Exposure to compressor oil mist should be minimized. Technicians must confirm suction line pressure before opening any fitting.

title: Spec Sheet: ZP Series Scroll Compressors
sourceText: The ZP series scroll compressor delivers higher efficiency across a wide range of condensing unit temperatures. Rated discharge pressure and subcooling targets are listed in Table 3.

title: Field Bulletin: Evaporator Frost Troubleshooting
sourceText: Evaporator frost is commonly caused by low refrigerant charge or restricted airflow. Measure superheat at the suction line before condemning the compressor.

title: Marketing One-Pager: Smart Diagnostics Platform
sourceText: Our smart diagnostics platform continuously monitors discharge pressure, superheat, and subcooling to flag issues before they become failures. No compressor teardown required.

title: Training Deck: Condensing Unit Startup Checklist
sourceText: Step 1: Confirm the condensing unit is level. Step 2: Verify suction line insulation is intact. Step 3: Record discharge pressure and compare against the spec sheet baseline.

title: Warranty Claim Form — Translated Fields
sourceText: List the compressor model number, condensing unit serial number, and date of installation. Attach photos of the refrigerant line set if a leak is suspected.
